subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw preserve the existing effective per-session serialization of context-engine `maintain()` calls after a timeout, or intentionally adopt concurrent/re-entrant calls as a new plugin contract?
rationale: The proposed timeout fixes a real stall, but it changes a public plugin behavior boundary. Choosing to impose concurrency on existing engines versus retaining host-side serialization is a maintainer-owned SDK compatibility decision.

options.title: Preserve serialization
options.body: Keep the timeout and host fence, but coalesce or defer successor plugin maintenance until the abandoned invocation settles.

options.title: Adopt re-entrant engine calls
options.body: Accept the new plugin contract only with explicit SDK approval, compatibility communication, and proof that bundled and supported external engines tolerate same-session overlap.

options.title: Pause for cancellation design
options.body: Hold this change until an additive cancellation/abort contract can terminate or safely isolate timed-out engine work.

recommendation.title: Preserve serialization
recommendation.body: Keep the timeout and host fence, but coalesce or defer successor plugin maintenance until the abandoned invocation settles.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice changes the public context-engine lifecycle contract rather than only repairing one scheduler call site.
